questions.knowledge_point: Estimating the Value of a Three-Variable Function
questions.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y,z)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(1,2,3)=3,\,{f}_{x}(1,2,3)=-2,\,{f}_{y}(1,2,3)=1,\,{f}_{z}(1,2,3)=3.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,2,3)$ estimate the value of $f(0.96,1.98,3.03).$
questions.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,2,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(1,2,3)+∇f(1,2,3)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z-3⟩ \\  & =f(1,2,3)+⟨{f}_{x}(1,2,3),{f}_{y}(1,2,3),{f}_{z}(1,2,3)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z-3⟩ \\  & =3+⟨-2,1,3⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(0.96,1.98,3.03)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=0.96,$ $y=1.98,$ and $z=3.03$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.96,1.98,3.03) & ≈3+⟨-2,1,3⟩\cdot ⟨0.96-1,1.98-2,3.03-3⟩ \\  & =3+⟨-2,1,3⟩\cdot ⟨-0.04,-0.02,0.03⟩ \\  & =3+0.08-0.02+0.09 \\  & =3.15\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Estimating the Value of a Three-Variable Function
questions.problem:
Let $f(x,y,z)$ be a differentiable function such that

$$
\begin{aligned} & f(3,0,4)=25, &  & {f}_{x}(x,y,z)=\frac{5x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}, \\  & {f}_{y}(x,y,z)=\frac{5y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}, &  & {f}_{z}(x,y,z)=\frac{5z}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3,0,4),$ estimate the value of $f(3.01,0.1,3.99).$
questions.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3,0,4)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(3,0,4)+∇f(3,0,4)\cdot ⟨x-3,y-0,z-4⟩ \\  & =25+⟨{f}_{x}(3,0,4),{f}_{y}(3,0,4),{f}_{z}(3,0,4)⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y,z-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(3,0,4)$, ${f}_{y}(3,0,4)$ and ${f}_{z}(3,0,4),$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(3,0,4) & =\frac{5(3)}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{4}^{2}}}=3 \\ {f}_{y}(3,0,4) & =\frac{5(0)}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{4}^{2}}}=0 \\ {f}_{z}(3,0,4) & =\frac{5(4)}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{4}^{2}}}=4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y,z)≈25+⟨3,0,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y,z-4⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(3.01,0.1,3.99)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=3.01,y=0.1$ and $z=3.99,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3.01,0.1,3.99) & ≈25+⟨3,0,4⟩\cdot ⟨3.01-3,0.1,3.99-4⟩ \\  & =25+⟨3,0,4⟩\cdot ⟨0.01,0.1,-0.01⟩ \\  & =25+0.03-0.04 \\  & =24.99\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Best Linear Approximation of a Multivariable Function
questions.problem: Let $f(x,y)=x{e}^{y}.$ Find the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2).$
questions.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)+∇f(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)\cdot ⟨x+1,y-\operatorname{ln}⁡2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the definition of $f,$ we have that $f(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)=-2.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x} & ={e}^{y}\, &  & ⇒\, & {f}_{x}(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}=2, \\ {f}_{y} & =x{e}^{y} &  & ⇒\, & {f}_{y}(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)=-1{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient of the function at the point $(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =⟨2,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the linear approximation of the function $f$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)+∇\,f(-1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-\operatorname{ln}⁡2⟩ \\  & =-2+⟨2,-2⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-\operatorname{ln}⁡2⟩ \\  & =-2+2(x+1)-2(y-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2+2x-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Estimating the Value of a Three-Variable Function
questions.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y,z)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(1,0,-1)=1,\,{f}_{x}(1,0,-1)=-1,\,{f}_{y}(1,0,-1)=-1,\,{f}_{z}(1,0,-1)=0.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,0,-1)$ estimate the value of $f(1.02,0.1,-0.96)$
questions.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,0,-1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(1,0,-1)+∇f(1,0,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-0,z-(-1)⟩ \\  & =f(1,0,-1)+⟨{f}_{x}(1,0,-1),{f}_{y}(1,0,-1),{f}_{z}(1,0,-1)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y,z+1⟩ \\  & =1+⟨-1,-1,0⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y,z+1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(1.02,0.1,-0.96)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=1.02,$ $y=0.1,$ and $z=-0.96$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.02,0.1,-0.96) & ≈1+⟨-1,-1,0⟩\cdot ⟨1.02-1,0.1,-0.96+1⟩ \\  & =1+⟨-1,-1,0⟩\cdot ⟨0.02,0.1,0.04⟩ \\  & =1-1(0.02)-1(0.1)+0(0.04) \\  & =1-0.02-0.1+0 \\  & =0.88\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Best Linear Approximation of a Multivariable Function
questions.problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=yz-x.$ Find the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(0,-1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(0,-1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(0,-1,1)+∇f(0,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x,y+1,z-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the definition of $f,$ we have that $f(0,-1,1)=-1.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x} & =-1\,⇒\,{f}_{x}(0,-1,1)=-1, \\ {f}_{y} & =z\,⇒\,{f}_{y}(0,-1,1)=1, \\ {f}_{z} & =y\,⇒\,{f}_{z}(0,-1,1)=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient of the function at the point $(0,-1,1)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(0,-1,1) & =⟨{f}_{x}(0,-1,1),{f}_{y}(0,-1,1),{f}_{z}(0,-1,1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the linear approximation of the function $f$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(0,-1,1)+∇f(0,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x,y+1,z-1⟩ \\  & ≈-1+⟨-1,1,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x,y+1,z-1⟩ \\  & ≈-1-(x)+(y+1)-(z-1) \\  & ≈1-x+y-z.\end{aligned}
$$
